title: Disproof by counter-example
body: is one line: find one $n$ that breaks the claim. Try $n=0,1,2$, a negative, a prime, a large number.

title: Even/odd bookkeeping
body: write even $=2k$, odd $=2k+1$. A square: odd$^2=4k(k+1)+1$, so **an odd square is always $1$ more than a multiple of $8$** (since $k(k+1)$ is even).

title: Consecutive integers
body: $n(n+1)$ is even; $n(n+1)(n+2)$ is a multiple of $6$; $(n-1)n(n+1)$ likewise.

title: Difference of squares
body: $a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)$ for proofs about differences of squares of consecutive numbers: $(n+1)^2-n^2=2n+1$.

title: Squares are never $\equiv2$ or $3\pmod 4$
body: ; they are $\equiv0$ or $1\pmod 4$. They are $0,1,4\pmod 8$ and $0,1,4,7\pmod9$ (beyond spec: modular arithmetic).

title: Proof by contradiction template (irrationality)
body: assume $\sqrt2=\dfrac pq$ in lowest terms, so $p^2=2q^2$, $p$ even, $p=2m$, $q^2=2m^2$, $q$ even — contradiction. Also works for "there are infinitely many primes".

title: Proof by exhaustion
body: list the finite cases (e.g. $n=1,2,3,4$) and check each.

title: To show a quadratic is always positive
body: complete the square or use $\Delta<0$.

title: Cover-up rule (linear distinct factors)
body: For $\dfrac{f(x)}{(x-a)(x-b)}=\dfrac A{x-a}+\dfrac B{x-b}$: $A=\dfrac{f(a)}{a-b}$. Cover $(x-a)$, substitute $x=a$ into what is left. $B$ likewise. **Gives answers in seconds and avoids simultaneous equations.**

title: Repeated factor
body: $\dfrac{f(x)}{(x-a)^2(x-b)}=\dfrac A{x-a}+\dfrac B{(x-a)^2}+\dfrac C{x-b}$: cover-up gives $B$ and $C$; $A$ from substituting any other value, or from the leading terms (compare $x^2$ coefficients).

title: Improper fraction (degree top $\ge$ bottom)
body: divide first; the quotient is a polynomial and the remainder is the proper fraction.

title: Quick check
body: substitute $x=0$ (or $x=1$) into both sides.

title: Telescoping
body: $\dfrac1{r(r+1)}=\dfrac1r-\dfrac1{r+1}$ and the general $\dfrac1{(x-a)(x-b)}=\dfrac1{a-b}\left(\dfrac1{x-b}-\dfrac1{x-a}\right)$.

title: Synthetic division
body: for $(x-a)$ (see P1). **Equate coefficients** for $(x^2+bx+c)$ style division: set quotient $=px+q$ and match.

title: Modulus graphs
body: reflect the part below the axis. $|f(x)|=k$: solve $f=k$ and $f=-k$. $|f(x)|<k\Leftrightarrow -k<f(x)<k$. $|x-a|<b\Leftrightarrow a-b<x<a+b$ ("distance from $a$ is less than $b$").

title: Two-modulus equations
body: $|f|=|g|$: square both sides, or solve $f=\pm g$.

title: Solving $|ax+b|=cx+d$
body: sketch first, then solve the two linear cases and **check for extraneous roots** (need $cx+d\ge0$).

title: Composite functions
body: $fg(x)=f(g(x))$, apply $g$ first. **Domain of $fg$** is the inputs of $g$ whose outputs lie in the domain of $f$.

title: Inverse
body: swap $x\leftrightarrow y$, solve. Graph is the reflection in $y=x$. **Domain of $f^{-1}$ = range of $f$.** Self-inverse functions satisfy $f(f(x))=x$ — e.g. $\dfrac{ax+b}{cx-a}$ and $\dfrac kx$.

title: Fixed points of the inverse
body: $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$ where $f$ is increasing $\Leftrightarrow f(x)=x$ (quicker than finding $f^{-1}$).

title: Transformation $y=f(ax+b)$
body: translate $y=f(x)$ **left by $b$**, then stretch parallel to the $x$-axis by factor $\dfrac1a$ (or stretch by $\dfrac1a$ first, then translate left by $\dfrac ba$).

title: $(a+bx)^n=a^n\left(1+\dfrac bax\right)^n$
body: Factor out $a^n$ **before** expanding; the validity condition is $|bx/a|<1$.

title: Fractional/negative $n$
body: valid only for $|x|<1$ (or $|bx/a|<1$). **Check this condition** — it is routinely examined.

title: Coefficient of one term only
body: use $\binom nr a^{n-r}b^r$ directly; the exponent of $x$ is $r$.

title: Approximating $\sqrt[n]{\cdot}$ values
body: write the number as $a(1+\epsilon)$, e.g. $\sqrt{101}=10\sqrt{1.01}=10\left(1+\tfrac12(0.01)-\tfrac18(0.01)^2\dots\right)$.

title: Binomial with an unknown coefficient $k$
body: match the required $x^r$ coefficient and solve for $k$; write the equation in terms of $k$ first, don't substitute numbers early.

title: Sum of binomial coefficients
body: $=2^n$; alternating sum $=0$; $\binom nr=\binom n{n-r}$.

title: Parametric to Cartesian
body: eliminate $t$. For $x=a\cos t$, $y=b\sin t$: $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ (ellipse). For $x=at^2$, $y=2at$: $y^2=4ax$.

title: Gradient
body: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$. **Normal** gradient $-\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$.

title: Circle parametrics
body: $x=a+r\cos t$, $y=b+r\sin t$.

title: Trig identities for elimination
body: $\cos^2+\sin^2=1$, $\sec^2=1+\tan^2$, $\cos2t=1-2\sin^2t$. If both $x$ and $y$ involve $\sin 2t$ and $\cos t$, use double-angle first.

title: Intersection of curves in parametric form
body: substitute the Cartesian equation of one into the parameter of the other.

title: Terms equidistant from the middle average to the middle term
body: For an odd number of terms, $S=n\times\text{middle term}$.

title: Common difference from two terms
body: $d=\dfrac{u_p-u_q}{p-q}$.

title: Sum of multiples of $k$ up to $N$
body: number of terms $=\lfloor N/k\rfloor$, sum $=k\cdot\dfrac{m(m+1)}2$ with $m=\lfloor N/k\rfloor$. Multiples of 3 or 5 (inclusion–exclusion): add multiples of 3 and of 5, subtract multiples of 15.

title: Three terms in AP
body: write them as $a-d,\,a,\,a+d$ (sum is $3a$ immediately). For four terms $a-3d,a-d,a+d,a+3d$.

title: Three terms in GP
body: write them $\dfrac ar,\,a,\,ar$ (product $=a^3$); the **middle term squared equals the product of the outer two**: $b^2=ac$.

title: Ratio from two terms
body: $r^{p-q}=\dfrac{u_p}{u_q}$.

title: Recurring decimals
body: $0.\dot a=\dfrac a9$, $0.\dot a\dot b=\dfrac{ab}{99}$, $0.\,x\dot a=\dfrac{xa-x}{90}$ (non-repeating digit then a repeating one: write as $x$ then the geometric tail).

title: Geometric sum of a block of terms
body: first term $\times\dfrac{1-r^{\text{number of terms}}}{1-r}$.

title: Convergence to a target
body: $|r|<1$. "Sum exceeds $N$" with $S_n=\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$: solve for $r^n$ then take logs (flip the inequality when dividing by $\ln r<0$).

title: Compound growth/decay and loans
body: the balance after $n$ years with yearly deposit $d$ at multiplier $m$ is a GP: $d\dfrac{m^n-1}{m-1}$ (first deposit gets $m^{n}$ or $m^{n-1}$ depending on timing — define it).

title: Limit of a convergent recurrence $u_{n+1}=f(u_n)$
body: set $L=f(L)$ and solve; reject the root outside the allowed range.

title: Periodic sequences
body: compute a few terms, find the period $p$, then $u_n=u_{n \bmod p}$ and $S_n=\lfloor n/p\rfloor S_p+S_{n\bmod p}$.

title: Three laws
body: $\log_ab+\log_ac=\log_a bc$; $\log_ab-\log_ac=\log_a\dfrac bc$; $k\log_ab=\log_ab^k$. **Also** $\log_ab=\dfrac{\log_cb}{\log_ca}$ and $\log_ab=\dfrac1{\log_ba}$.

title: Change of base shortcut
body: $a^{\log_b c}=c^{\log_b a}$ (swap base and argument); $\log_{a^n}b^m=\dfrac mn\log_ab$.

title: $\log_a1=0$, $\log_aa=1$, $a^{\log_ax}=x$
body: Convert $\log_ax=y\Leftrightarrow x=a^y$ at once.

title: Solve $a^{f(x)}=b$
body: by taking logs: $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln b}{\ln a}$ — write the exact form, then decimals at the end.

title: Mixed bases
body: put all logs in one base before collecting; $\log_2x+\log_4x=3$ gives $\log_2x+\tfrac12\log_2x=3$.

title: Solve $\log_ax+\log_a(x-k)=m$
body: combine, make the quadratic, **reject roots outside the domain** ($x>0$, $x-k>0$).

title: Reduce to linear to find constants
body: $y=ab^x\Rightarrow\log y=\log a+x\log b$ (straight line, gradient $\log b$, intercept $\log a$). $y=ax^n\Rightarrow\log y=\log a+n\log x$ (plot $\log y$ against $\log x$; gradient $n$).

title: Exponential growth/decay
body: $N=N_0e^{kt}$; doubling time $=\dfrac{\ln2}k$; half-life $=\dfrac{\ln2}{|k|}$. **Percentage change per time unit** $=e^k-1$.

title: Rule of 72 (approximation)
body: doubling time $\approx\dfrac{72}{\text{percentage rate}}$ years.

title: Large powers without a calculator
body: $\log_{10}2\approx0.301$, $\log_{10}3\approx0.477$, $\log_{10}7\approx0.845$. Number of digits in $N$ is $\lfloor\log_{10}N\rfloor+1$. First digit from the fractional part of the log.

title: Derivatives
body: $\dfrac d{dx}e^{kx}=ke^{kx}$, $\dfrac d{dx}a^x=a^x\ln a$, $\dfrac d{dx}\ln x=\dfrac1x$, $\dfrac d{dx}\ln f(x)=\dfrac{f'}{f}$ (**logarithmic derivative**).

title: Addition formulae
body: $\sin(A\pm B)=\sin A\cos B\pm\cos A\sin B$; $\cos(A\pm B)=\cos A\cos B\mp\sin A\sin B$; $\tan(A\pm B)=\dfrac{\tan A\pm\tan B}{1\mp\tan A\tan B}$.

title: Double angles (three versions of $\cos2A$)
body: $\sin2A=2\sin A\cos A$; $\cos2A=\cos^2A-\sin^2A=2\cos^2A-1=1-2\sin^2A$; $\tan2A=\dfrac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2A}$.

title: Rearrange for powers
body: $\cos^2A=\dfrac{1+\cos2A}2$, $\sin^2A=\dfrac{1-\cos2A}2$ — gold for integrating $\cos^2$, $\sin^2$.

title: Half-angle tangent
body: $t=\tan\dfrac\theta2$: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$, $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}$ (beyond spec; turns $a\sin\theta+b\cos\theta=c$ into a quadratic).

title: Triple angle
body: $\sin3A=3\sin A-4\sin^3A$; $\cos3A=4\cos^3A-3\cos A$ (beyond spec but frequently proven in exams).

title: Product → sum and sum → product (beyond spec)
body: $2\sin A\cos B=\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)$; $2\cos A\cos B=\cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)$; $2\sin A\sin B=\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)$; $\sin P+\sin Q=2\sin\dfrac{P+Q}2\cos\dfrac{P-Q}2$; $\cos P+\cos Q=2\cos\dfrac{P+Q}2\cos\dfrac{P-Q}2$.

title: $a\sin x+b\cos x=R\sin(x+\alpha)$
body: with $R=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, $\tan\alpha=\dfrac ba$ (**$\cos\alpha=\dfrac aR$, $\sin\alpha=\dfrac bR$: fix the quadrant**).

title: Maximum $R$, minimum $-R$
body: Max occurs when $x+\alpha=90^\circ$. Equation $a\sin x+b\cos x=c$ has solutions iff $|c|\le R$.

title: Alternatives
body: $R\cos(x-\beta)$ with $\tan\beta=\dfrac ab$. Choose the form that matches what the question wants.

title: Minimum/maximum of $\dfrac1{k+a\sin x+b\cos x}$
body: from the harmonic form's extremes.

title: Exact values to know
body: $\sin15^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}4$, $\cos15^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}4$, $\tan15^\circ=2-\sqrt3$, $\tan75^\circ=2+\sqrt3$.

title: $\sin18^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}4$, $\cos36^\circ=\dfrac{1+\sqrt5}4$
body: (pentagon values, beyond spec).

title: Equations with $\sin2x$ and $\sin x$
body: factorise $2\sin x(\cos x-\dots)$; don't divide by $\sin x$.

title: Reciprocals
body: $\sec=\dfrac1{\cos}$, $\operatorname{cosec}=\dfrac1{\sin}$, $\cot=\dfrac1{\tan}$; $\sec^2=1+\tan^2$, $\operatorname{cosec}^2=1+\cot^2$.

title: Inverse trig ranges
body: $\arcsin\in[-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2]$, $\arccos\in[0,\pi]$, $\arctan\in(-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2)$. $\arcsin x+\arccos x=\dfrac\pi2$.

title: Small angles
body: $\sin\theta\approx\theta$, $\cos\theta\approx1-\dfrac{\theta^2}2$, $\tan\theta\approx\theta$ (radians). Used to simplify limits and approximations.

title: Radians
body: arc $=r\theta$, sector $=\tfrac12r^2\theta$, segment $=\tfrac12r^2(\theta-\sin\theta)$. Convert: $\times\dfrac\pi{180}$.

title: Chain rule fast
body: differentiate the outside, keep the inside, multiply by the derivative of the inside. $\dfrac d{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\,g'(x)$. Linear inside: just multiply by its gradient.

title: Product rule
body: $(uv)'=u'v+uv'$. **Quotient rule:** $\left(\dfrac uv\right)'=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$.

title: Reciprocal of a function
body: $\dfrac k{f}=kf^{-1}$, so $\dfrac d{dx}\dfrac k{f}=-\dfrac{kf'}{f^2}$ with no quotient rule; $\dfrac1{(2x+1)^3}=(2x+1)^{-3}$ is a plain chain rule.

title: Logarithmic differentiation (products/powers)
body: $y=x^x$, $y=\dfrac{(x+1)^3(x-2)^2}{x^5}$: take $\ln$ first: $\dfrac{y'}y=\dots$ (beyond spec at some levels).

title: Differentiate $a^x$
body: $a^x\ln a$.

title: Standard derivatives
body: $(\sin x)'=\cos x$, $(\cos x)'=-\sin x$, $(\tan x)'=\sec^2x$, $(\sec x)'=\sec x\tan x$, $(\operatorname{cosec}x)'=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x$, $(\cot x)'=-\operatorname{cosec}^2x$, $(\ln x)'=\dfrac1x$, $(e^{kx})'=ke^{kx}$.

title: Implicit differentiation
body: differentiate each term in $x$; every $y$-term gets $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ attached; collect, factor, divide. Example: $x^2+y^2=r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac xy$. $xy$ → $y+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

title: Parametric
body: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\dot y}{\dot x}$; second derivative $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\Big/\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ (not $\ddot y/\ddot x$).

title: Inverse derivative
body: $\dfrac{dx}{dy}=\dfrac1{dy/dx}$.

title: Connected rates
body: $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{dA}{dr}\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. Quote the formula for the quantity first, differentiate with respect to the variable, then use the chain rule.

title: Gradient of the inverse at a point
Stationary point nature
body: $f''$; if $f''=0$ use the sign of $f'$ either side.

title: Points of inflection
body: $f''=0$ and $f''$ changes sign.

title: Newton–Raphson
body: $x_{n+1}=x_n-\dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$; $\sqrt a$: $x_{n+1}=\tfrac12\left(x_n+\dfrac a{x_n}\right)$.

title: Fixed-point iteration
body: write $f(x)=0$ as $x=g(x)$; converges when $|g'(x^*)|<1$: a **staircase** diagram when $0<g'<1$, a **cobweb** when $-1<g'<0$.

title: Small changes
body: $\delta y\approx\dfrac{dy}{dx}\,\delta x$ — error propagation, percentage error: $\dfrac{\delta y}y\approx n\dfrac{\delta x}x$ for $y\propto x^n$.

title: Reverse chain rule (inside is linear)
body: $\int f(ax+b)\,dx=\dfrac1aF(ax+b)+c$. $\int e^{kx}=\dfrac{e^{kx}}k$; $\int\dfrac1{ax+b}=\dfrac1a\ln|ax+b|$; $\int\sin(kx)=-\dfrac{\cos kx}k$; $\int\cos(kx)=\dfrac{\sin kx}k$; $\int\sec^2(kx)=\dfrac{\tan kx}k$.

title: "The derivative is on top" recognition
body: $\int\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}dx=\ln|f(x)|+c$; $\int f'(x)\,[f(x)]^n\,dx=\dfrac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}+c$; $\int f'(x)e^{f(x)}dx=e^{f(x)}+c$. Spot these before reaching for substitution.

title: Trig powers
body: $\sin^2$ and $\cos^2$ via double angle; $\sin^3x=\sin x(1-\cos^2x)$ then substitute $u=\cos x$ (**odd power: peel off one factor**); $\tan^2=\sec^2-1$; $\sin x\cos x=\tfrac12\sin2x$.

title: Products of sines/cosines
body: product-to-sum formulas (see §6).

title: Typical substitutions
body: $\sqrt{ax+b}\to u=\sqrt{ax+b}$ (or $u^2=ax+b$); $\sqrt{1-x^2}\to x=\sin\theta$; $\dfrac1{1+x^2}\to x=\tan\theta$ so $\int=\arctan x$; $\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\arcsin x$ (beyond spec at some levels).

title: Even simpler for linear-over-root
body: $\int\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}}dx$: set $u=x+1$ so $x=u-1$.

title: Log alone
body: $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-x+c$ ($u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$).

title: Cyclic by parts
body: ($e^x\sin x$): apply twice; the original reappears; solve for it: $\int e^{ax}\sin bx\,dx=\dfrac{e^{ax}(a\sin bx-b\cos bx)}{a^2+b^2}$ and $\int e^{ax}\cos bx\,dx=\dfrac{e^{ax}(a\cos bx+b\sin bx)}{a^2+b^2}$.

title: Tabular (DI) method
body: for $\int x^n e^{kx}$, $\int x^n\sin kx$: differentiate $x^n$ down to zero, integrate the other factor repeatedly, alternate signs $+,-,+,\dots$ and multiply diagonally. $\int x^2e^{x}dx=e^{x}(x^2-2x+2)+c$.

title: Check
body: differentiate your result.

title: Area between curves
body: $\int(\text{top}-\text{bottom})\,dx$; the parabola/chord one-sixth shortcut $\dfrac{|a|(\beta-\alpha)^3}6$ (see P1).

title: Volume of revolution about the $x$-axis
body: $\pi\int y^2\,dx$; about the $y$-axis $\pi\int x^2\,dy$. **Washer:** $\pi\int(R^2-r^2)\,dx$.

title: Standard volumes
body: sphere $\tfrac43\pi r^3$, cone $\tfrac13\pi r^2h$, frustum from the two-cone difference; the volume of a cap of height $h$ on a sphere radius $r$: $\pi h^2\left(r-\dfrac h3\right)$.

title: Separable differential equations
body: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=f(x)g(y)\Rightarrow\int\dfrac1{g(y)}dy=\int f(x)\,dx$. **Add $+c$ on one side only; use the initial condition at once.** $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=ky\Rightarrow y=Ae^{kx}$.

title: Trapezium rule
body: $\tfrac h2[y_0+y_n+2\sum y_i]$ (over/under: curve bending up ⇒ over). **Simpson's rule (beyond spec):** $\dfrac h3\left[y_0+y_n+4(\text{odd})+2(\text{even})\right]$ with an **even number of strips**; exact for cubics.

title: Integral of a modulus
body: split at the zero of the inside function.

title: Symmetric limits
body: odd function over $[-a,a]$ gives $0$; even gives twice the half.

title: King's property (beyond spec)
body: $\int_a^bf(x)\,dx=\int_a^bf(a+b-x)\,dx$ — often turns $\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$ into $\tfrac\pi4$ by adding the two forms.

title: Famous results to know
body: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2x\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^2x\,dx=\dfrac\pi4$; $\int_0^1x^n\,dx=\dfrac1{n+1}$; $\int_0^\infty e^{-x}dx=1$.

title: Differentiate any integral to check; integrate numerically (trapezium with 2 strips) to check definite integrals
Substitute $x=0,1$
body: to verify partial fractions and series.

title: Logs and exponents
body: test with an easy value, e.g. $x=2$ in $\log_2x$.

title: Trig
body: check a special angle ($30^\circ,45^\circ$).

title: Factor out a supplied intersection
body: If a line and a quadratic meet at a known $x=a$, form their difference $D(x)$ and divide by $x-a$; the remaining linear factor gives the second intersection without a quadratic formula. Check $D(a)=0$ before dividing and substitute the second root into both original equations.

title: Record exclusions before clearing denominators
body: For a rational equation, list every forbidden value from the original denominators before multiplying by a common denominator; cancellation can hide an excluded root. Check each candidate against those exclusions and the original equation, especially if a factor was cancelled.

title: Separate a coefficient from its term
body: In a binomial question asking for the coefficient of $x^r$, calculate the multiplier of $x^r$ and report that number alone; retain the $x^r$ factor only while locating the term. Check the question's wording before the final line.

title: Use the output range to prune a composite equation
body: When $f(g(x))=c$ has several algebraic candidates for $g(x)$, discard any outside the actual range of $g$ before solving for $x$. Check the domain of $f$ as well; for example, $g(x)=x^2$ cannot supply a negative intermediate value.

title: Horizontal chord from its half-length
body: For a horizontal chord of length $L$ in $(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2$, its endpoint has $|x-h|=L/2$, so $|y-k|=\sqrt{r^2-(L/2)^2}$. Choose $y=k+\cdots$ or $k-\cdots$ from the diagram, and check $L\le2r$.

title: Circle radius reality check
body: In $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$, calculate $r^2=g^2+f^2-c$ before describing a real circle or tangent. Check $r^2>0$ for a genuine circle, $r^2=0$ for one point, and $r^2<0$ for no real locus.

title: Parametric elimination keeps its range
body: After eliminating $t$, carry the given parameter interval into restrictions on $x$ and $y$; $x=t^2$ with $t\ge0$ gives $t=\sqrt{x}$, not both square-root signs. Check one endpoint and the direction of travel against the Cartesian curve.

title: Convert the gradient fully to the parameter
body: For a tangent or normal at parameter $t=u$, simplify $dy/dx$ into a function of $t$ and evaluate at $u$ before building the line. Check that the line passes through $(x(u),y(u))$ and that its gradient uses the same parameter value.

title: Arc length can replace the sector angle
body: If a sector's arc length $s$ and radius $r$ are known, use $A=\tfrac12rs$ directly, since $s=r\theta$ and $A=\tfrac12r^2\theta$ for radians. Check that $s$ is the curved arc, not the chord, and that the result has square units.

title: Restrict the harmonic maximum to the given interval
body: After writing $a\sin x+b\cos x=R\sin(x+\alpha)$, do not automatically claim the maximum on a restricted interval is $R$. Test the interval endpoints and every in-range point with $x+\alpha=\pi/2+2\pi k$; the largest of those values is the required maximum.

title: Find a sinusoid from its extremes
body: If a graph or context gives maximum $M$ and minimum $m$, set amplitude $R=(M-m)/2$ and midline $d=(M+m)/2$ before finding phase or period. Check that $d+R=M$ and $d-R=m$; this avoids solving for several coefficients at once.

title: Track radians through derivatives
body: Standard trig derivatives such as $d(\sin x)/dx=\cos x$ assume $x$ is measured in radians; convert degree data to radians before differentiating a trig model. Check that an angle of $180^\circ$ enters as $\pi$, while a final angle may be converted back if requested.

title: Read the first indexed term, not the displayed multiplier
body: For $\sum_{j=p}^{\infty}aq^j$, substitute the actual starting index $p$ to get the first term before using $S_\infty=\text{first}/(1-q)$. Check the next term divided by the first equals $q$ and that $|q|<1$.

title: Count gaps rather than data points
body: If a trapezium table has $m$ equally spaced ordinates, it has $m-1$ strips and width $h=(b-a)/(m-1)$. Check that the first and last $x$ values differ by exactly $(m-1)h$ before applying the weights.

title: Protect the interior trapezium sum with brackets
body: Write $T=\tfrac h2[y_0+y_n+2(y_1+\cdots+y_{n-1})]$ with a visible bracket around every interior ordinate before entering it into the calculator. Check that endpoints have weight $1$ and every interior value has weight $2$.

title: Delay rounding a sequence parameter
body: When an AP or GP is used in later parts, retain the exact common difference or ratio and calculate later sums from it, not from a rounded intermediate decimal. Check the first two reconstructed terms against the original data.

title: Test a proposed sum by finite differences
body: If $S_n$ is claimed to sum terms $u_1,\ldots,u_n$, compute $S_n-S_{n-1}$ and see whether it simplifies to $u_n$. Also check $S_1=u_1$; these two tests detect an index shift without re-summing the series.

title: Differentiate a factorised product at a root
body: If $f(x)=(x-a)g(x)$ and only the tangent gradient at $x=a$ is needed, use $f'(a)=g(a)$; all terms containing $x-a$ vanish. Check that $f(a)=0$ so the tangent passes through $(a,0)$.

title: Bound an area before calculating it
body: If $a<b$ and $m\le f(x)\le M$ on $[a,b]$, then $m(b-a)\le\int_a^bf(x)\,dx\le M(b-a)$; for a positive integrand this gives an instant size check. Confirm the bounds really hold throughout the interval, not just at its endpoints.
